Remark 4.10. From Proposition 4.7 , it follows that the middle optimum $(\mathbf{O}_1+\mathbf{O}_2)/2$ is
not a minimum of the map $\mathbf{O}_3 \mapsto \lambda_3(\mathbf{O}_1,\mathbf{O}_2,\mathbf{O}_3)$ when $\|\mathbf{O}_1 - \mathbf{O}_2\|$ is large enough. Hence,
for all $\|\mathbf{O}_1-\mathbf{O}_2\|$ large enough, by symmetry, the map $\lambda_3(\mathbf{O}_1,\mathbf{O}_2,\cdot)$ has at least two differ-
ent minima, of the type $(\pm a_\beta,0,\dots,0)$ , for a certain $a_\beta > 0$ , under the notation . For
all $\|\mathbf{O}_1-\mathbf{O}_2\|$ large enough, these optima maximise the difference $\lambda_2(\mathbf{O}_1,\mathbf{O}_2) - \lambda_3(\mathbf{O}_1,\mathbf{O}_2,\cdot)$
(which is positive, by Proposition 4.6 ).
